memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 31‑year‑old vegetable vendor reports painful swollen joints in hands and feet for 2 months, associated morning stiffness >1 hour, and scaly plaques on elbows and knees.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82, weight 92 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 32.6 (obese). Tender swollen MCP and PIP joints bilaterally, mild synovitis of knees. Psoriatic plaques erythematous with silvery scale on extensor surfaces.
IMPRESSION: Active rheumatoid arthritis (likely seropositive) with comorbid plaque psoriasis and obesity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start methotrexate 10 mg PO weekly, folic acid 5 mg weekly, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD, prednisolone 5 mg OD. Topical clobetasol 0.05% cream BD to plaques, calcipotriol ointment OD. Advise weight reduction, low‑purine diet, regular exercise. Return if worsening joint pain, fever >38.5°C, new rash, or abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports reduced joint swelling and morning stiffness now ~30 min; psoriasis plaques slightly less scaly. Complains of mild nausea after methotrexate.
EXAMINATION: BP 126/80, weight 89 kg, BMI 31.5 (obese). Joints less tender, no effusions. Psoriasis plaques pink‑white, scaling decreased.
IMPRESSION: Partial response to DMARDs; mild methotrexate nausea.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue methotrexate 10 mg weekly, folic acid 5 mg weekly; add folic acid 5 mg OD on day after methotrexate to reduce nausea. Maintain hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD, taper prednisolone to 2.5 mg OD. Continue topical agents. Reinforce diet and activity. Return if joint pain worsens, nausea persists, or liver enzymes rise.

memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes increased fatigue and mild joint discomfort in wrists; psoriasis stable.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84, weight 88 kg, BMI 31.2 (obese). Mild synovitis of wrists, no nodules. Skin lesions unchanged.
IMPRESSION: Inadequate disease control; consider escalating DMARD therapy.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase methotrexate to 15 mg weekly, keep folic acid 5 mg weekly plus post‑MTX folic acid 5 mg OD. Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD, prednisolone 2.5 mg OD. Add monthly liver function monitoring. Advise weight loss goal 5 kg in 3 months. Return if worsening pain, new rash, or abdominal discomfort.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports worsening morning stiffness lasting 45 min, mild scalp scaling, and fatigue.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82, weight 86 kg, BMI 30.4 (obese). Tenderness in MCP joints, mild scalp erythema with scaling.
IMPRESSION: Active rheumatoid arthritis with worsening psoriasis; obesity persists.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop prednisolone due to lack of benefit and risk of side‑effects. Increase methotrexate to 20 mg weekly, continue folic acid 5 mg weekly plus post‑MTX folic acid 5 mg OD. Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD. Add topical betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% cream BD to scalp plaques. Reinforce diet, aim for 7 kg loss. Return if joint swelling increases, fever, or liver enzymes rise.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: X‑ray of both hands (PA view): Juxta‑articular osteopenia, mild narrowing of MCP joint spaces, no erosions noted. Soft tissue swelling present. No bony destruction. Impression: Early rheumatoid arthritis changes, no significant joint damage yet.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral outcome from Rheumatology: Patient reviewed, advised to continue methotrexate 20 mg weekly with folic acid, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD. Consider adding low‑dose prednisolone 5 mg alternate days if flare persists. Psoriasis managed with topical steroids; consider phototherapy if no improvement. LFTs monitored monthly. Return to primary care for routine follow‑up.
